before.question: Which statement is most accurate? Focus: treatment goals.
choices: Current nucleos(t)ide analog therapy suppresses HBV replication and reduces progression risk but rarely eradicates covalently closed circular DNA.
Promising a routine short curative course can encourage unsafe discontinuation.
Assume viral suppression removes every need for monitoring, vaccination, or cancer surveillance.
Select therapy from drug name alone without kidney, bone, liver, pregnancy, resistance, coinfection, or adherence context.
before.rationale: Current nucleos(t)ide analog therapy suppresses HBV replication and reduces progression risk but rarely eradicates covalently closed circular DNA. Set goals for durable DNA suppression, biochemical improvement, fibrosis protection, and prevention of cirrhosis, decompensation, transmission, and cancer.

after.question: Which statement is most accurate? Focus: treatment goals.
choices: Oral nucleos(t)ide analogs suppress replication; undetectable serum HBV DNA does not prove elimination of nuclear cccDNA
An undetectable serum HBV DNA result proves all infected hepatocytes have been cleared
Polymerase inhibition routinely produces rapid sterilizing cure of chronic HBV
Normal ALT after treatment establishes that HBV-related cancer risk is zero
after.rationale: Polymerase inhibition can suppress replication while the nuclear reservoir persists. Serum DNA, ALT and liver-risk assessment describe different outcomes; none alone establishes eradication or freedom from every future liver complication.
